affectedSurfaces: security-review no-op outcome and commit gating
hypothesis: Resolving confirmed findings by the stable finding-id and candidate-id pair across all task states, while merging distinct run provenance into one canonical record, prevents repeated reviews from creating redundant actionable tasks without suppressing distinct title collisions or losing historical evidence.

metricsCompared.name: canonical tasks after replaying one stable finding across two review runs
metricsCompared.baseline: Two differently worded ready task records were materialized for the same finding and candidate identity.
metricsCompared.candidate: One canonical record retains both run ids; the explicit superseded record remains unchanged as historical evidence.

metricsCompared.name: mutations on an identical subsequent replay
metricsCompared.baseline: Title-slug and terminal-state resolution could allocate or rewrite follow-up work without a stable provenance-current signal.
metricsCompared.candidate: Zero task mutations and zero commit-preparation steps; the workflow reports confirmed-findings-current.

metricsCompared.name: focused security-review regression suite
metricsCompared.baseline: Terminal findings were expected to allocate suffixed ready tasks and no canonical/superseded replay fixture existed.
metricsCompared.candidate: 22 of 22 focused tests pass across creation, stable identity, terminal state, explicit supersession, collision, and workflow replay paths.

rationale: The candidate replaces title-slug coincidence with a strict stable identity, preserves the strongest existing priority and all distinct review run ids, fails closed on multiple unsuperseded canonical records, and keeps exact title collisions distinct. Focused behavioral tests, type checking, formatting, diff hygiene, and source-size limits pass; task-queue validation passes with zero errors and warnings against an isolated exact-path projection of the workflow host's staging transition.
